moves.comment: Take space in the centre and open the diagonals of your queen and f1 bishop. The reply decides which part of your White repertoire to follow.

children.comment: Occupy the centre with a second pawn. The d4 pawn will support an advance of the e-pawn.
Close the centre with a supported pawn on e5. You gain space, but the base of your pawn chain on d4 will need protection.
Support the d4 pawn with your c-pawn. Black is attacking the base of your pawn chain, so reinforce it before starting a wing attack.
Bring your knight to f3. From f3 it controls d4 and e5. Keep watching Black's replies before advancing more pawns.
Bring your bishop to e2. It supports your knight on f3.

Advance with support from the d4 pawn. Black can develop the light-square bishop before playing the e-pawn, unlike the usual French structure.
Develop the king-side knight to support d4 and e5. The opposing light-square bishop is already outside the pawn chain, so do not treat this as the same French position.
